header.sense_verification_rule: sense_verified=true ONLY when ALL hold: (a) the dump relation carries NO sense text (sense-agnostic), (b) the headword has exactly ONE sense (one definition) in the seed, (c) the dump entry POS maps to the seed partOfSpeech. Relations with a Korean sense gloss cannot be matched to the seed's English (NIKL) glosses without translation, so they go to sense_unverified. Multi-sense headwords and POS mismatches are likewise unverified. Unverified rows are NOT merge rows; they are a review list.

review_signals.mutual_in_dump_note: Target's own Korean-Wiktionary entry lists the headword back under the same kind. Confirms the relation exists in Wiktionary from both sides; does NOT verify the sense against our seed entry.
review_signals.seed_gloss_overlap_note: Distinctive English content words shared between the headword's and the target's seed (NIKL/v1) definitions. REVIEW-PRIORITISATION SIGNAL ONLY -- never a verification, never a merge criterion on its own. Tokenised lowercase, light stemming (ing/ed/es/s stripped), standard + generic-gloss stopwords removed.

manual_review.reviewed: all 271 strict-rule verified rows, by hand against the seed's English glosses (verified_review.txt)
manual_review.reason_summary: The automated strict rule (sense-agnostic + single-sense headword + POS match) cannot catch the case where the DUMP relation belongs to a Wiktionary sense our seed entry does not carry. The target's own seed gloss exposes it: e.g. 구매->사기 is real only for 사기='buying', but our 사기='morale'. 83 rows demoted for target-sense mismatch (most), outright wrong pair, loose association, or not-an-opposite. 3 of the 30 spot-check sampled rows were among the demoted ones (구매->사기, 긍정->부정, 일본->왜) -- the spot-check confirms dump presence, NOT sense fitness.
seed_gloss_bugs_found: 악 glossed as 'what energy that one musters up' (should be 'evil') -- affects 죄->악; fix the 악 seed gloss before using that relation.
공원 glossed as 'a person who works at a factory' (should be 'park') -- affects 뜰->공원.
